issues.label: Appellate jurisdiction and finality
issues.why: The court must confirm it has jurisdiction over a final, appealable order and proper notice of appeal.

issues.label: Appeal scope after jury trial
issues.why: The court must decide whether denial of summary judgment is reviewable after a full trial and verdict or is mooted by the trial record.

issues.label: Standard of review: summary judgment
issues.why: If reviewable, the court must apply de novo review under Civ.R. 56 and construe evidence most strongly for the nonmovant.

issues.label: Standard of review: JMOL
issues.why: If the challenge is to sufficiency at trial, the court must apply Civ.R. 50 standards to preserved motions for directed verdict/JNOV.

issues.label: Standard of review: weight of evidence
issues.why: If raised, the court must apply manifest-weight review and consider credibility deference to the jury.

issues.label: Preservation of error
issues.why: The court must determine which issues were preserved by objections, Civ.R. 50 motions, or proposed instructions/interrogatories.

issues.label: Harmless error analysis
issues.why: For any error, the court must decide whether it affected substantial rights and warrants reversal.

issues.label: R.C. 2745.01 exclusivity/threshold
issues.why: The court must apply Ohio’s narrow employer-intentional-tort statute and its heightened intent requirement.

issues.label: Employee status and course of employment
issues.why: Liability requires plaintiff to be an employee acting within the course and scope of employment.

issues.label: Intent to injure requirement
issues.why: Absent the presumption, plaintiff must prove actual intent to injure or statutory “substantial certainty” as defined.

issues.label: Meaning of substantial certainty
issues.why: The court must apply R.C. 2745.01(B)’s definition equating substantial certainty with deliberate intent.

issues.label: Applicability of 2745.01(C)
issues.why: The court must determine whether the rebuttable presumption is available on these facts.

issues.label: Define equipment safety guard
issues.why: The court must decide whether the PTO shaft guard and/or PTO coupling guard qualifies as an “equipment safety guard” under Ohio law.

issues.label: Guard part of equipment vs workplace
issues.why: The court must determine whether the guard is an integral machine guard (covered) rather than a general workplace safety measure (not covered).

issues.label: Identify which guard matters
issues.why: The court must determine whether the claimed removal concerns the shaft guard, coupling guard, or both, and how that affects causation/presumption.

issues.label: Meaning of deliberate removal
issues.why: The court must interpret whether “deliberate removal” includes only affirmative acts or can include failure to repair/replace a missing guard.

issues.label: Failure to replace as removal
issues.why: The central statutory question is whether knowingly operating equipment without replacing a guard equals deliberate removal.

issues.label: Temporary removal for repair
issues.why: The court must decide whether removal during maintenance that is not replaced constitutes deliberate removal.

issues.label: Removal by employer vs third party
issues.why: The presumption requires removal “by an employer,” so the court must decide if a contractor’s removal (if any) is attributable to the employer.

issues.label: Authorization or direction to remove
issues.why: Even if others removed the guard, the court must decide whether employer authorization constitutes employer removal.

issues.label: Knowledge of missing guard
issues.why: The court must consider whether employer knowledge of the guard’s absence supports deliberate decision-making and intent elements.

issues.label: Duration of missing guard
issues.why: Evidence that the guard was missing for a long time may bear on deliberateness, rebuttal, and causation.

issues.label: Employer control over equipment
issues.why: The court must consider whether Gill Dairy had control and responsibility for maintaining guards on its machinery.

issues.label: Rebuttable presumption operation
issues.why: The court must correctly apply how the presumption shifts burdens (production/persuasion) and what must be rebutted.

issues.label: Rebutting intent presumption
issues.why: The court must decide whether Gill Dairy produced sufficient evidence to rebut presumed intent and whether the jury instruction properly framed it.

issues.label: Burden of proof on intent
issues.why: The court must ensure the jury was instructed that plaintiff retains ultimate burden, even with a presumption, consistent with statute and evidence rules.

issues.label: Causation: direct result under (C)
issues.why: The court must determine whether injury occurred as a direct result of the guard’s removal, not merely general unsafe conditions.

issues.label: Proximate cause at common law
issues.why: Independently, plaintiff must prove proximate cause linking employer conduct to injury.

issues.label: Intervening cause/employee conduct
issues.why: The court must assess whether plaintiff’s actions (turning machine on to inspect) break causation or constitute comparative negligence (if relevant).

issues.label: Comparative negligence applicability
issues.why: The court must decide whether comparative negligence is a defense to statutory employer intentional tort or irrelevant given intent-based liability.

issues.label: Assumption of risk defense
issues.why: The court must determine whether primary/secondary assumption of risk is barred or limited in intentional tort context.

issues.label: Employer’s safety warnings impact
issues.why: The court must consider how manufacturer warnings and employer communications bear on intent, deliberateness, and rebuttal.

issues.label: OSHA evidence admissibility
issues.why: The court must decide whether OSHA reports/statements were properly admitted and for what purpose (notice, causation, intent).

issues.label: Hearsay within OSHA report
issues.why: The court must analyze hearsay issues, including admissions by party-opponent and public-records exceptions.

issues.label: BWC report admissibility
issues.why: The court must evaluate admissibility and permissible uses of BWC investigative materials and embedded statements.

issues.label: Authentication of video/image
issues.why: The court must ensure the March 2018 video image was properly authenticated and relevant to condition at injury time.

issues.label: Evidence of prior condition
issues.why: The court must decide whether evidence from 2018 supports inference of condition in 2019 without undue speculation.

issues.label: Inference stacking concerns
issues.why: The court must ensure verdict is not based on impermissible speculative inferences about who removed the guard and when.

issues.label: Corporate knowledge and agency
issues.why: The court must attribute acts/knowledge of owners/managers to LLC for “employer” intent and conduct.

issues.label: Which actor removed the guard
issues.why: The court must decide whether evidence permits a reasonable finding that Gill Dairy (through its agents) removed the guard.

issues.label: Sufficiency for deliberate removal
issues.why: The court must decide whether evidence at trial was legally sufficient to support the jury’s finding of deliberate removal.

issues.label: Sufficiency for causation finding
issues.why: The court must decide whether evidence supports the finding that removal proximately caused the injury.

issues.label: Sufficiency for failure to rebut
issues.why: The court must decide whether evidence supports the jury’s finding that employer did not rebut the presumption of intent.

issues.label: Consistency of interrogatories/verdict
issues.why: The court must determine whether the general verdict and interrogatory answers are consistent and what remedy applies if not.

issues.label: Interrogatory majority requirement
issues.why: The court must ensure the verdict/interrogatories satisfied Ohio’s civil jury concurrence rules (e.g., 3/4 of jurors) and were properly polled/recorded.

issues.label: Proper instruction on intent
issues.why: The court must assess whether instructions correctly stated R.C. 2745.01’s intent standard and did not dilute it into negligence/recklessness.

issues.label: Proper instruction on presumption
issues.why: The court must decide whether telling the jury it “may but is not required” to infer intent accurately conveys a rebuttable presumption.

issues.label: Definition of deliberate removal
issues.why: The court must assess whether the instruction’s definition (remove/lift/push aside/eliminate) properly captures statutory meaning and case law.

issues.label: Instruction on direct result
issues.why: The court must decide whether “direct result” was properly explained so jury linked injury to absence of guard.

issues.label: Allocation of burdens in instruction
issues.why: The court must ensure the instructions and interrogatories correctly allocated burden to defendant only as to rebuttal, not ultimate liability.

issues.label: Evidentiary prejudice from alteration
issues.why: The court must consider whether evidence of the altered “quote/invoice” was admissible and whether it improperly suggested liability beyond spoliation/credibility.

issues.label: Spoliation-related spillover
issues.why: Although spoliation claim failed, the court must assess whether spoliation evidence unfairly prejudiced the intentional tort verdict.

issues.label: Punitive/damages limitations
issues.why: The court must confirm compensatory damages were properly categorized and not barred/limited by statute or workers’ compensation principles.

issues.label: Workers’ compensation exclusivity
issues.why: The court must ensure the claim fits within the narrow intentional-tort exception to workers’ compensation exclusivity.

issues.label: Economic vs noneconomic damages proof
issues.why: The court must assess whether the evidentiary support and instructions for damages (medical, wage loss, pain) were legally adequate.

issues.label: Excessive damages/remittitur
issues.why: If raised, the court must evaluate whether the award is excessive, against the weight, or influenced by passion or prejudice.

issues.label: Civ.R. 59 new trial grounds
issues.why: If a new trial motion was made, the court must assess claimed trial errors under the proper standard.

issues.label: Post-trial judgment entry
issues.why: The court must confirm the judgment properly reflects the verdict, interrogatories, and any statutory requirements.

issues.label: Statutory interpretation methodology
issues.why: The court must interpret R.C. 2745.01(C) consistent with Ohio Supreme Court precedent and legislative intent to narrow employer intentional torts.

issues.label: Application to agricultural machinery
issues.why: The court must decide whether PTO guarding fits within prior precedent on “safety guard” and “removal” in similar industrial contexts.
